expected_evidence: Geological: platinum, iridium, and other siderophile-element anomalies in a well-dated ~12,900 BP boundary layer across North American and global sediment sequences
Geological: nanodiamonds, magnetic microspherules, and meltglass/impact spherules in the Younger Dryas Boundary (YDB) black mat layer
Geological: sharp charcoal/soot spike indicating continental-scale biomass burning coincident with YD onset
Geological: ice-core (e.g., Greenland GISP2/GRIP) chemical/particulate anomalies dated to the YD onset
Astronomical: orbital/dynamical modeling showing the Taurid meteor stream's debris field and Earth-crossing geometry ca. 10,950 BCE consistent with a dense encounter
Astronomical: identification of a plausible fragmenting parent body or crater(s) (e.g., proposed Hiawatha Glacier crater) datable to the same interval
Material/archaeological: abrupt disruption or hiatus in Clovis-culture site occupation layers directly beneath/at the black mat horizon
Material/paleontological: megafaunal extinction markers (bone bed terminations, dung fungus Sporormiella decline) clustering at the same horizon
Genetic: population bottleneck or extinction signatures in ancient DNA of North American megafauna and early human populations dated to ~10,950 BCE
Oral tradition: indigenous North American narratives describing sky-fire, darkness, or catastrophic cold events (highly speculative, hard to date/verify)
Model-prior: consistency with independently modeled Taurid stream density peaks recurring on multi-millennial cycles
response.rationale: This hypothesis sits at the Pleistocene/Holocene transition, spanning the tail of the Upper Paleolithic and the Younger Dryas boundary itself, so both period rows are relevant; I weight toward 'younger-dryas' since the claimed event IS the onset of that stadial. The strongest expected evidence channels are geological (0.6-0.65 detectability: ice cores, sediment boundary layers, black mats — well preserved and already the subject of an active real-world scientific literature, the 'Younger Dryas Impact Hypothesis' associated with Firestone et al. and later platinum-anomaly studies) and astronomical (0.7: orbital modeling of the Taurid stream is a modern reconstructive method not dependent on ancient preservation, so it is highly detectable in principle). Material archaeological evidence (Clovis disruption, megafaunal extinction markers) has moderate detectability (0.35) since Upper Paleolithic North American sites are sparse and taphonomically poor. Genetic evidence is weaker (0.25-0.3) given degraded ancient DNA from this era. Textual (0.0) and linguistic (0.05) evidence are essentially impossible this far back — no writing systems existed, so their total absence is fully explained by detectability, not by falsity. Oral tradition and iconographic evidence are low (0.1) — any surviving Indigenous narratives would have undergone millennia of transmission distortion, making them suggestive at best, not confirmatory. Given that this claim (a Taurid-stream/cosmic-impact trigger for the Younger Dryas onset) is itself a real, actively debated hypothesis in the literature with claimed physical correlates (platinum spikes, nanodiamonds, black mats) that were sought and partially reported — though heavily contested for replicability and alternative explanations (volcanism, terrestrial processes) — I flag this as a `model-prior`-informed judgment. Overall I set the detectability adjustment at 0.55, reflecting that the highest-value evidence types (geological, astronomical) are quite detectable and have in fact been actively searched, while archaeological/genetic/textual/oral corroboration remains structurally limited by the deep time depth and pre-literate context — so weak or contested archaeological evidence should not be read as strong evidence against the hypothesis.
